exposure: initiated breastfeeding in the first hour of life
cohort: The study included 265 neonates with a median age of 4 days, admitted to the special care unit at Kawempe National Referral Hospital in Uganda.
finding: The prevalence of neonatal sepsis was 35.8%, with significant factors associated with it including delivery from a peripheral clinic, maternal perinatal pyrexia, meconium stained liquor, poor cord care, and prelacteal feeding.
mod_finding: Neonates delivered by caesarean section were associated with lower chances of getting neonatal sepsis (aOR = 0.4, 95% CI = 0.2, 09, P = .02).
followup_time: at least 4 days (median age of neonates at data collection)
